10: # 1. Overview
11: 
12: The default method by which SQLite implements
13: atomic commit and rollback is a rollback journal .
14: Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new "Write-Ahead Log" option
15: (hereafter referred to as "WAL") is available.
16: 
17: There are advantages and disadvantages to using WAL instead of
18: a rollback journal. Advantages include:
19: 
20: WAL is significantly faster in most scenarios.
21: 
22: WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and
23: a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed
24: concurrently.
25: 
26: Disk I/O operations tends to be more sequential using WAL.
27: 
28: WAL uses many fewer fsync() operations and is thus less vulnerable to
29: problems on systems where the fsync() system call is broken.
30: 
31: But there are also disadvantages:
32: 
33: All processes using a database must be on the same host computer;
34: WAL does not work over a network filesystem. This is because WAL requires
35: all processes to share a small amount of memory and processes on
36: separate host machines obviously cannot share memory with each other.
37: 
38: Transactions that involve changes against multiple ATTACHed
39: databases are atomic for each individual database, but are not
40: atomic across all databases as a set.
